Polemoniaceae.key_door: fused 5-part flower + 5 epipetalous stamens + superior 3-locular ovary → 3-valved capsule

Primulaceae.key_door: stamens opposite corolla lobes + free-central placentation; Lysimachia superior vs Samolus semi-inferior ovary

Styracaceae.key_door: Halesia vs Styrax by bud scales, pith, shoot age, ovary position and fruit wings

Symplocaceae.key_door: alternate simple leaves + many epipetalous stamens + inferior ovary + persistent-calyx drupe

Fouquieriaceae.key_door: petiolar spines + rain-flushed leaf fascicles + red tubular flower + 10–16+ stamens + 3-valved capsule

anchor_families.Sapotaceae: woody fused-flower/fruit comparison with latex + hard seed

taxonomy_notes: Samolus valerandi subsp. parviflorus is a synonym of accepted Samolus parviflorus and should not be double-counted.
Giliastrum incisum, Giliastrum rigidulum, Ipomopsis rubra, Phlox drummondii and Phlox pilosa remain accepted current concepts; Phlox pilosa subsp. riparia remains accepted.
Halesia diptera, Styrax platanifolius, Symplocos tinctoria and Fouquieria splendens remain accepted current concepts.
Lysimachia arvensis remains accepted but is an introduced Old World comparison in the Texas learner.
guardrails: Family/genus recognition only; no species promotion.
Do not use taste as an ID test for Symplocos.
Fouquieria splendens Texas nativity does not imply Hays County nativity; strict local-range judgments remain in species workflows.
